editions.text:
The day added up to 22 species, 18 heard and 12 seen, across 113 feeder visits, which is below the past week's average of 195.4 visits and below its average of 259.6 heard detections. The species count matched the week's average of 21.9, and visits were higher than only two of the seven prior days. Tufted Titmouse led the visits with 47, and Eastern Towhee led the detections with 54.

Eleven species were recorded on all seven days, this one included, among them Eastern Towhee, Tufted Titmouse, Carolina Chickadee, Blue Jay and Northern Cardinal. Red-shouldered Hawk and American Goldfinch, which were recorded on five and four of the prior days, were not recorded today. Northern Cardinal was the first visual of the day at 24 min before sunrise and the last at 11 min after sunset.

The audio source changed many times through the day, moving between c120, pi and pi-mic (movo-dom1), so the heard counts came from whichever source was active at each point. No species was heard for the first time at this station today, and no first confident visual record was made. Hairy Woodpecker was heard once, at 15:00, and was recorded on three of the seven days, including this one.
